scripts.title: Scripts to narrate
scripts.description: The batch: an array of script objects, one voiceover file per item. Each item: "text" (required — the words to narrate, up to 100,000 characters; long texts are split into sentence chunks automatically), "title" (optional — names the output file and row), "voice" (optional — overrides the global Voice for this item only). One bad item never stops the batch: it returns an ERROR row and is not charged. Example item: {"title": "Intro", "text": "Welcome to the show.", "voice": "Easton"}

prefill.title: Welcome message
prefill.text: Welcome to Batch Voiceover Studio. This sample was generated entirely on a CPU, with no API key and no GPU.

prefill.title: Product teaser
prefill.text: Turn a list of scripts into finished voiceovers in one run. One flat rate per thousand characters, thirty-seven voices to choose from, and audio files you can download straight away.

voice.title: Voice
voice.description: The narrator voice for every script in the batch (a script can override it with its own "voice"). 37 English voices from the Phonon catalog: American and British narrators plus character voices (pirate captain, wizard, dragon and more). Harper is a modern, confident, friendly American voice — a safe default for explainers and ads.

outputFormat.title: Output format
outputFormat.description: Audio file format for every voiceover in the batch: MP3 (compact, ready for video editors and podcast tools) or WAV (lossless 24 kHz, for further editing). The dataset row's audioUrl points at the finished file either way.
